$comment: What this corpus was read against, and what has been published since.
Every rule here carries effective_from, and the resolver evaluates against
a date — but all 54 carry effective_to: null, and none carries a
supersedes pointer. So the engine treats every rule as in force forever,
and an evaluation dated today is served with a citation and no caveat.
That is fine while nothing has superseded them and dangerous the moment
something has. MPD-2047 was notified on 2026-08-20 and this corpus does
not contain a single rule from it. A tool whose whole claim is that its
numbers are traceable must also say how current the thing it traced to is.
DELIBERATELY NOT A SUPERSESSION CLAIM. The English gazette was searched
in full and no operative transition provision was located — no 'in
supersession of', no commencement clause, no date on which MPD-2021
ceases. Asserting that MPD-2021 stopped governing on 2026-08-20 would be
precisely the confidently-wrong answer this product exists to avoid. What
is stated below is what can be shown from the documents themselves: what
we read, and what we have not.
Resolving this needs a person to read the transition provisions and the
DDA FAQ, then either date-bound these rules or record why they still
stand. Until then the honest position is that we do not know.

read_against.label: MPD-2021
read_against.note: Compilation incorporating modifications up to 31 August 2022.

unread_successors.label: MPD-2047
unread_successors.source: Stated on page 1 of the gazette: 'approved by the Central Government under Section 11A(2) of DD Act 1957 and notified vide Gazette Notification S.O. No. 4597(E) dated 20.08.2026.'
unread_successors.note: Registered in sources.json with its hash; no rule has been extracted from it. Its effect on any value below has not been established.
